1: The door back out to Warrior City.
Y: A window, open a crack for the air.
H: The apothecary's shelves: willow bark, mint, and something labelled DO NOT.
The DO NOT is nearly empty.
b: A bed, made very tightly. It won't be empty long.
d: A bed, and somebody in it.
P: A bench by the door, worn smooth by families waiting.

objects.name: Oren
lines: You're up and about. Good.
Oren. I've been sitting here a while. The ward is full of people who were strong once. I sit with them. Sit, if you like.

objects.name: Healer Maud
lines: Sit if you're hurt. Stand if you're not. Go away if you're both.
...Sorry. Fourteen beds. Twelve full. I haven't sat down since the last culling games.

answer: Three sleepers this month. Wandered in out of cocoons, they say, not knowing the year.
We feed them soup and tell them gently. The soup helps more than the telling.
Nobody. The bank pays the strong. These aren't, any more. That's rather the point of them being here.
I mend them, and the city sends them north. I try not to mend them too quickly.

questions.ask: Bit grumpy for a healer, aren't you?
answer: I've a bedside manner. It's for people in beds.
You're standing. Go away.

objects.name: Orderly Bede
lines: I'm not a healer. I carry things. Water, bandages, bad news.
Mostly bad news. It's the lightest, and somehow the hardest to put down.

objects.name: Champion Bruck
lines: Don't fuss. I'm not hurt. I'm resting standing up. Champions do that.
The arm? That's how it goes now. It's a new style.

answer: It's bent. Bent is a kind of strong. Ask a bow.
If I'm hurt, the stipend stops, and my mother stops being a goddess, and we all go north. So I'm not hurt.

questions.ask: Let the healer look at it.
answer: She has looked at it. She made a face. I've decided the face meant 'magnificent'.

questions.ask: Push-ups, then. Go on. Show me.
answer: I'll do them later. When there's more room. And another arm.

objects.name: Private Tam
lines: Shield arm. Snapped clean in the yard.
They say it'll set. They also say there's no stipend for a soldier who can't hold a shield. I'm learning to hold it with my teeth.

answer: Get better before the bank notices.
Or move north, to the camp, with my mum. She's already packed. Everyone's mum is already packed.

questions.ask: Can't hold a shield? Some soldier.
answer: I held it fine. It was the other fellow's hammer that didn't stop where it was meant to.

objects.name: Sergeant Holm
lines: Zzz... five hundred... one day... zzz...
...I was there. On the island. I don't talk about it awake.

objects.name: Private Ivo
lines: Knee. I was the fastest runner in my year.
Now I'm the fastest limper on the ward. It doesn't pay. I asked.

objects.name: Corporal Hett
lines: Twenty years in the line. One bad landing, and the bank's struck me off by the afternoon.
They're quick, the bank. Quicker than the healing.

answer: North. There's a camp for people like me. Deserters, they call us.
I never deserted anything. It deserted me. Started with the knee.
I saved plenty. The bank keeps it. You only get it back if you're strong enough to ask.

objects.name: Sigi
lines: Seventeen. I was going into the Kaloseum next spring, for the culling games.
Now I'm not going anywhere. Except north, Mum says. She's been very brave about it. Louder than usual.

objects.name: Osk the Wall
lines: They called me the Wall. Walls don't fall over.
Turns out they do, if you hit them enough. Who knew. Everybody, apparently. Everybody but me.

objects.name: Old Corran
lines: Forty years a soldier. The longest anyone's lasted in the line.
Thirty-nine of them, I was strong. They don't count those. They only count this one.

answer: A granddaughter. She's twelve next month. They'll take her to the Yard.
If she's strong, she stays. If she's not, she comes north with me. I'm hoping for strong. I'm packing for both.

questions.ask: Forty years and you still got hurt?
answer: Forty years and I only got hurt the once. You try it.

objects.name: Dag
lines: Hit my head in the yard. I keep forgetting I'm not strong any more.
Then I remember. It's worse, the remembering. I'd like to forget it again.

objects.name: Big Haldor
lines: Zzz... more stew... zzz...
...not hurt... zzz... resting... like Bruck...

objects.name: Ilka
lines: Sigi's mum. He'll tell you I'm brave. I'm not. I'm loud. It passes for brave in this city.
We'll be gone by the new moon. North. I've knitted him a scarf. They say it's cold, at the camp.

questions.ask: Is there nothing that can be done?
answer: He could get strong again. Before the bank's next count.
So I've brought him soup, and I'm knitting faster. It's all a mother can do here, unless you're a goddess.
He trained every day since he was twelve. Every day. In the snow.
Go and stand somewhere else.

objects.name: Brin and Bet
lines: We're waiting for Dad. He's the Wall.
He fell over. Mum says walls don't, but he did, so now we know.
